sentences.text: Gallardosaurus was a marine predator with a short neck that possessed a broad, low skull equipped with long, pointed teeth.
Evidence of unfused vertebrae indicates the known specimen was a juvenile when it died.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 1946 by Cuban farmer Juan Gallardo near Viñales in northwestern Cuba.

The genus Gallardosaurus was formally described as a separate genus in 2009, and the name honors the fossil's discoverer, Juan Gallardo, while the species name iturraldei honors the paleontologist Dr. Manuel Iturralde-Vinent.
Researchers suggest Gallardosaurus likely migrated seasonally across the Caribbean Sea and primarily ate nectonic fish.
Gallardosaurus inhabited shallow waters approximately 10 to 12 meters deep, a habitat colonized by oysters and algae.
Gallardosaurus is classified as a pliosaurid within the family Pliosauridae, a group that includes Hauffiosaurus, Kronosaurus, Peloneustes, Liopleurodon, Brachauchenius, and Pliosaurus.
Fossils of Gallardosaurus come from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Jagua Formation in western Cuba, where the animal lived between 159 and 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
